question.problem:
Consider the vector subspace $H=\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\}.$ Which of the following vectors belong to ${H}^{⊥}?$

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let  $h=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ A vector $v$ belongs to ${H}^{⊥}$ if $v$ is orthogonal to $h.$ So, we have to find the products ${v}_{i}\cdot h$ for $i=1,2,3.$  

- For ${v}_{1}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot h & =1\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 3=10\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, ${v}_{1}\notin {H}^{⊥}.$

- For ${v}_{2}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2}\cdot h & =(-3)\cdot (-1)+2\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot 3=-4\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, ${v}_{2}\notin {H}^{⊥}.$

- For ${v}_{3}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\cdot h & =(-2)\cdot (-1)+4\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 3=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, ${v}_{3}\in {H}^{⊥}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${v}_{3}$ only".
